meta.title: CMMS SaaS Server Development Roadmap
meta.description: Development broken into stable, testable increments. Each chunk is self-contained with enough context to be executed independently.

chunks.name: Core Kernel & Module System
chunks.description: Build the microkernel that discovers, validates, boots, and supervises modules. Zero business logic.
chunks.prompt: Implement the CORE module at /src/server/core/ with: (1) ModuleBase abstract class with name, version, dependencies, optional_dependencies, profiles, and async methods configure(), initialize(), start(), stop(), health(). (2) Service registry with register_service(name, port, interface) and get_service(name, interface) with type checking. (3) Event bus with async publish(event, payload, post_commit=False) and subscribe(event, handler, post_commit=False), isolating subscriber failures so one failing listener never breaks others. (4) Settings loader parsing CMMS_<MODULE>__<KEY> env vars into per-module pydantic Settings objects, failing boot on invalid config. (5) Dependency graph validator detecting cycles (raise DependencyCycleError with cycle_path) and unknown dependencies. (6) Topological sort using Kahn's algorithm with alphabetical tie-break. (7) Boot orchestration: discover modules from package, validate graph, topological order, filter by profile (api|worker|beat|mcp|all-in-one), then run configure()->initialize(ctx)->start() in order, logging each module name+version. (8) Shutdown in reverse order with drain. (9) Health polling: async poll_health(timeout_s) calling every module's health() concurrently, reporting UNAVAILABLE on timeout. (10) Supervision loop: poll_health, propagate degradation (if hard dep is UNAVAILABLE, dependent modules become DEGRADED), apply restart policy, emit module.health_changed events. (11) Utilities: utcnow() (tz-aware, never use datetime.now directly), new_id() (UUID4), new_request_id() (short unique string). (12) Feature flags via CMMS_FEATURE_<FLAG> env (default false). (13) Structured JSON logger with module namespacing and request_id correlation. Deliver working kernel that can boot a dummy module set and detect dependency cycles.

chunks.name: Infrastructure Layer - DB, Cache, Storage, Email
chunks.description: Infrastructure adapters: PostgreSQL with RLS, Redis services, object storage abstraction, transactional email.
chunks.prompt: Implement four infrastructure modules at /src/server/modules/{db,cache,storage,email}/. DB module: (1) build_engine() creating async SQLAlchemy engine from CMMS_DB__URL with POOL_SIZE, MAX_OVERFLOW, POOL_TIMEOUT, STATEMENT_TIMEOUT. (2) session_factory() for platform-level sessions. (3) org_scoped_session(org_id) context manager executing SET LOCAL app.organization_id = :org on BEGIN for PostgreSQL RLS. (4) ensure_extensions() creating vector, pgcrypto, citext extensions. (5) run_migrations(revision) for programmatic alembic upgrade. (6) transaction(session) context manager committing on success, rolling back on exception. (7) register_models(module_name, base) collecting models for migration autogeneration, enforcing organization_id column on tenant tables. (8) health_check() returning HealthReport with connectivity ping and pool saturation %. CACHE module: (1) connect() returning async Redis client from CMMS_CACHE__URL with retry. (2) allow(key, limit, window_s) sliding-window rate limiter returning RateDecision{allowed, remaining, reset_at}. (3) lock(name, ttl_s, wait_ms=0) safe-release distributed lock using SET NX PX + Lua compare-and-delete. (4) delay_schedule(task_name, payload, run_at) ZADD for delayed jobs. (5) delay_due(now) atomically popping due jobs via ZPOPMIN. (6) kv_get/kv_set/kv_delete for short-lived cache. (7) broker_url() for Celery. (8) health_check() with PING + latency + memory. STORAGE module: (1) backend() selecting adapter by CMMS_STORAGE__BACKEND (local|minio|s3). (2) tenant_key(org_id, category, *parts) building '/org-{org_id}/{category}/...' paths, rejecting '..' and absolute segments. (3) put(key, stream, mime, max_bytes) streaming upload with SIZE_EXCEEDED abort. (4) get(key) streaming download. (5) delete(key) idempotent delete. (6) exists(key) head object. (7) presigned_url(key, ttl_s=900, method='GET') with max 1h TTL. (8) sniff_mime(head) using python-magic. (9) health_check() write-read-delete probe. EMAIL module: (1) provider() selecting adapter by CMMS_EMAIL__PROVIDER (smtp|api). (2) render(template, vars) producing RenderedEmail{subject, html, text} for verify_email|password_reset|invitation templates. (3) send(to, subject, html, text) with 3 retries exponential backoff, redacting addresses except domain. (4) send_template(template, to, vars) as main entrypoint. (5) health_check() provider handshake. All modules must implement ModuleBase protocol and report health.

chunks.name: API Surface & Worker Engine
chunks.description: HTTP surface (FastAPI factory, middleware chain, error envelope) and Celery task engine with idempotency.
chunks.prompt: Implement API and WORKER modules at /src/server/modules/{api,worker}/. API module: (1) create_app() FastAPI factory with title/version, OpenAPI at /api/v1/openapi.json (toggle via CMMS_API__OPENAPI_ENABLED), central exception handlers, no static file mounts. (2) register_router(router, prefix, tags) mounting under /api/v1, raising on duplicate prefix. (3) add_middleware(factory, order) registering middleware sorted by order at startup. (4) install_middleware_chain() with fixed order: request_id(10)->cors(20)->auth_hook(30)->org_scope_hook(40)->rate_limit(50). (5) error_handler(request, exc) mapping domain exceptions to status codes (QuotaExceeded->403 TIER_LIMIT_REACHED, NotFound->404, Forbidden->403, PaymentOverdue->403 ORG_PAYMENT_OVERDUE), returning {error_code, message, details} envelope, never leaking stack traces. (6) paginate(stmt, page=1, page_size=50) applying LIMIT/OFFSET + COUNT, clamping page_size 1..200. (7) require(action, resource=None) endpoint guard delegating to AUTH.rbac_can. (8) request_context() dependency extracting verified claims into RequestContext{org_id, user_id, role, request_id, timezone}. (9) cors_config() from CMMS_API__CORS_ORIGINS with credentials true. (10) serve(host, port, workers) uvicorn helper. WORKER module: (1) create_celery_app() with broker/result from CACHE.broker_url(), JSON serializer, task time limits. (2) register_task(name, fn, retry=None) wrapping with logging, failure-reason persistence, retry policy. (3) register_beat(name, task_name, schedule) adding to beat registry. (4) dispatch(task_name, args=None, countdown=None, idempotency_key=None) acquiring CACHE lock if idempotency_key given, returning existing task_id if already running. (5) task_status(task_id) returning TaskStatus{state, result, error, started_at, finished_at}. (6) single_flight(name, ttl_s) cluster-wide exactly-one-at-a-time via CACHE.lock. (7) retry_with_backoff(task, exc, base=2.0, max_retries=5) exponential backoff with jitter, routing to dead-letter on exhaustion. (8) failed_jobs(page, page_size) returning dead-letter entries. (9) collect_contributions(modules) calling each module's register_tasks()/register_beat() at start(). (10) drain(timeout_s) graceful shutdown. Both modules must implement ModuleBase and report health.

chunks.name: Authentication & Authorization
chunks.description: Identity management: signup, login, JWT lifecycle, password flows, RBAC engine feeding API auth hook.
chunks.prompt: Implement AUTH module at /src/server/modules/auth/ with tables: users, roles, user_organization_memberships(read-only), auth_refresh_tokens, email_verification_tokens, password_reset_tokens. Functions: (1) signup(email, password, timezone='UTC') route POST /auth/signup: validate password policy, hash with Argon2id, create unverified user, create single-use verification token (24h), send verify_email template via EMAIL, emit user.registered, return 201 with generic message on duplicate. (2) verify_email(token) route POST /auth/verify-email: validate single-use time-limited token, mark user verified, emit user.verified, 204 on success. (3) login(email, password) route POST /auth/login: verify credentials, block unverified/deactivated users, rate-limit via CACHE, issue JWT access token (15m, HS256, claims {sub:user_id, organization_id, role, jti, exp}) and refresh token (7d, HttpOnly Secure cookie), emit user.logged_in with ip/user_agent. (4) refresh(refresh_cookie) route POST /auth/refresh: rotation invalidating presented token and issuing new one in same family; REUSE detection (already-rotated token presented) invalidates entire family + force re-login. (5) logout() route POST /auth/logout: revoke current refresh token family, clear cookie. (6) forgot_password(email) route POST /auth/forgot-password: if user exists create single-use reset token (30min) + email, constant response to prevent enumeration, rate-limited. (7) reset_password(token, new_password) route POST /auth/reset-password: validate token, update hash, invalidate all sessions via invalidate_user_sessions, mark token used, emit user.password_reset. (8) me(ctx) route GET /auth/me: return Profile{user, membership, organization, role, permissions[]}. (9) issue_access_token(user_id, org_id, role) -> signed JWT. (10) verify_access_token(token) -> Claims verifying signature/exp/jti-not-revoked. (11) hash_password(pw) / verify_password(pw, hashed) using Argon2id. (12) password_policy(pw) returning violation codes (min 10 chars, upper+lower+digit+symbol, reject breached list). (13) rbac_can(ctx, action, resource=None) implementing permission matrix (role x action) + object-level rules, deactivated users always False. (14) require_roles(*roles) FastAPI dependency. (15) auth_hook(request) middleware order 30: extract Bearer token -> verify_access_token -> store claims on request.state, public route list bypasses. (16) invalidate_user_sessions(user_id) revoking all refresh families + adding active jti to revocation list (CACHE kv with TTL=access token lifetime). (17) change_role(ctx, user_id, new_role) route PATCH /auth/roles (MANAGER/SYS_ADMIN only): restricted role change, cannot grant SYS_ADMIN via org APIs, audited, emit user.role_changed. (18) deactivate_user(ctx, user_id) blocking new actions/assignments, retaining history, invalidating sessions, audited, emit user.deactivated. (19) sweep_expired_tokens() task beat=daily: delete expired verification/reset/refresh rows. Emit events: user.registered, user.verified, user.logged_in, user.password_reset, user.role_changed, user.deactivated. Depends on core, db, cache, email, api.

chunks.name: Tenancy & Organization Management
chunks.description: Organizations, membership, tier/quota enforcement, payment state gate, invitations.
chunks.prompt: Implement TENANCY module at /src/server/modules/tenancy/ with tables: organizations, organization_custom_fields, user_organization_memberships, invitations, subscription_tiers, payment_states. Functions: (1) create_organization(ctx, data) route POST /tenancy/orgs (SYS_ADMIN or first-org free): create org with profile {name, logo, contact, timezone, custom_fields{}}, create root zone linked to org, emit org.created. (2) get_organization(ctx, org_id) route GET /tenancy/orgs/{id}: org-scoped fetch. (3) update_organization(ctx, org_id, patch) route PATCH /tenancy/orgs/{id} (MANAGER): update profile, audited, emit org.updated. (4) can_create_ticket(org_id) -> bool: check payment_state != OVERDUE, used by TICKETS gate. (5) can_create_service_point(org_id) -> bool: check tier quota (Free<=100, Pro<=1000, Ultimate=unlimited), count active service_points, raise QuotaExceeded if exceeded. (6) get_tier_quota(tier_name) -> int: return quota for tier. (7) send_invitation(ctx, org_id, email, role) route POST /tenancy/invitations (MANAGER): create invitation row with single-use token (14d expiry), send invitation template via EMAIL, emit invitation.sent. (8) accept_invitation(token) route POST /tenancy/invitations/accept: validate token, add user to org membership, if user has existing membership handle replacement (leave old org), emit invitation.accepted. (9) expire_invitations() task beat=hourly: soft-delete expired invitations, emit invitation.expired. (10) get_membership(ctx, user_id) -> Membership: return current org membership with role. (11) change_membership(ctx, user_id, org_id, role) (MANAGER/SYS_ADMIN): update membership, audited, emit membership.changed. (12) record_payment_overdue(org_id) / clear_payment(org_id): update payment_state, emit payment.overdue/cleared. (13) org_scoped_query(session, org_id) helper ensuring all queries filter by organization_id. Events emitted: org.created, org.updated, invitation.sent, invitation.accepted, invitation.expired, membership.changed, payment.overdue, payment.cleared. Depends on core, db, api, auth, email, worker.

chunks.name: Asset Hierarchy - Zones, Systems, Service Points
chunks.description: Asset hierarchy CRUD, counters, QR codes, safety flags, zone cloning, inheritance logic.
chunks.prompt: Implement ASSETS module at /src/server/modules/assets/ with tables: zones, zone_custom_fields, systems, system_zone_links, sub_systems, service_points, asset_qr_codes, counters, counter_logs, safety_flags. Functions: (1) create_zone(ctx, data) route POST /zones (MANAGER): validate depth (max 2 under zone), create zone with profile {name, parent_id, status, address, contact, description, custom_fields{}, geolocation}, enforce TENANCY.can_create_service_point for quota if counting toward limit, emit asset.zone.created, audited. (2) update_zone(ctx, zone_id, patch) route PATCH /zones/{id} (MANAGER): update profile, audited, emit asset.zone.updated. (3) decommission_zone(ctx, zone_id) route DELETE /zones/{id} (MANAGER): soft-decascade children to INACTIVE/DECOMMISSIONED, retain history, emit asset.zone.decommissioned. (4) create_system(ctx, data) route POST /systems (MANAGER): create system with {name, classification, specs}, link to zones via system_zone_links (one primary), depth max 2 (system/sub-system), emit asset.system.created. (5) update_system / decommission_system similar. (6) create_service_point(ctx, data) route POST /service-points (MANAGER): validate TENANCY quota, create node with {name, code, system_id, status=ACTIVE, qr_id}, emit asset.service_point.created. (7) update_service_point / decommission_service_point similar. (8) assert_depth(entity_type, parent_id) raising MAX_DEPTH_EXCEEDED if total hierarchy >6 levels or zone breakdown >2 or system depth >2. (9) create_counter(ctx, node_id, data) route POST /service-points/{id}/counters (MANAGER): create counter {type:HOURS|COUNT, unit, inherit_from_parent, influence_child_nodes}, multiple counters per node allowed. (10) log_counter(ctx, counter_id, new_value, reason) route POST /service-points/{id}/counters/log (OPERATOR,MANAGER): write counter_logs{prev, new, logged_by, reason, source=MANUAL}, if influence_child_nodes propagate top-down to child counters with source=INHERITED, emit counter.logged, audited. (11) reset_counter(ctx, counter_id, scope:NODE|NODE_AND_CHILDREN) route POST /service-points/{id}/counters/reset (MAINTENANCE where permitted): reset to 0 with source=RESET, never affect unrelated parents, audited, emit counter.reset. (12) counter_logs(ctx, counter_id, page, page_size) route GET /service-points/{id}/counters/logs: full change history. (13) effective_counter(node_id, counter_type) -> Counter: resolve inheritance chain top-down, used by CYCLES. (14) generate_qr(ctx, node_id) route POST /service-points/{id}/qr (MANAGER): stable code per node, server-side PNG generation via STORAGE under qr/, persist asset_qr_codes row, return QrAsset{code, image_key}. (15) resolve_qr(ctx, code) route GET /qr/resolve/{code}: resolve node, return QrView{profile, history, manuals, attachments, active_work_orders, active_tickets} with sections filtered by caller role, 404 on unknown code. (16) print_label(ctx, node_id) route GET /service-points/{id}/qr/label: HTML/PDF printable label with QR + node identity. (17) clone_zone(ctx, zone_id) route POST /zones/{id}/clone (MANAGER): create clone job, dispatch WORKER task, return CloneJob{id, status:PENDING}. (18) run_clone(job_id) task: replicate zone tree, profiles, custom fields, system links, service points, cycles, template assignments, config with NEW IDs and unique codes, states PENDING->PROCESSING->COMPLETED|FAILED, emit asset.zone.cloned, notify. (19) set_safety_flag(ctx, node_id, flag, on) route POST /service-points/{id}/flags (MANAGER,MAINTENANCE): flag in {HOT_INSPECT, PAUSE_FOR_INSPECTION, STOP_UNTIL_COMPLETE}, persist + audit + emit safety_flag.changed, MCP agent may never clear/downgrade human-set STOP_UNTIL_COMPLETE. (20) effective_flags(node_id) -> FlagState{own_flags, propagated_to_parents[], halted_parents[]}: compute propagation - flags affect parent structure, only maintenance-halt flags stop parents. (21) for_node_view(ctx, node_id) -> NodeAggregate: port used by MCP resources. Events: asset.zone.created/updated/decommissioned/cloned, asset.system.created/updated/decommissioned, asset.service_point.created/updated/decommissioned, counter.logged/reset, safety_flag.changed. Depends on core, db, api, tenancy, storage, worker.

chunks.name: Templates - Workflows & Checklists
chunks.description: Workflow/checklist templates, item-level search, unique codes, immutable snapshots for work orders.
chunks.prompt: Implement TEMPLATES module at /src/server/modules/templates/ with tables: workflows, workflow_items, checklist_templates, checklist_items. Functions: (1) create_workflow(ctx, data) route POST /workflows (MANAGER): auto-generate org-unique code if absent, validate items via validate_item_graph, persist header+items, emit template.created, audited. Data includes {name, description, code?, items[]} where each item has {activity_number, predecessor?, description, dates?, status, priority, durations?, assignee/skills/certs/tools/parts placeholder, safety_permit?, risk?, location_override?, measurement_fields?, signature_required?, cost?, downtime?, notes}. (2) get_workflow(ctx, workflow_id) route GET /workflows/{id}: org-scoped fetch with items. (3) update_workflow(ctx, workflow_id, patch) route PATCH /workflows/{id} (MANAGER): header update, code changes re-checked for uniqueness, NEVER affects existing work orders (snapshot semantics), audited, emit template.updated. (4) list_workflows(ctx, q=None, page, page_size) route GET /workflows: org-scoped paginated list. (5) archive_workflow(ctx, workflow_id) route DELETE /workflows/{id} (MANAGER): soft-delete (deleted_at, is_active=false), blocked if referenced by ACTIVE cycles unless reassigned, audited, emit template.archived. (6) add_workflow_item(ctx, workflow_id, item) route POST /workflows/{id}/items (MANAGER): validate predecessor refs exist within same workflow and graph stays acyclic, measurement thresholds only for NUMERIC. (7) update_workflow_item / delete_workflow_item similar validations, soft-delete items. (8) create_checklist(ctx, data) route POST /checklists (MANAGER): flat inspection items with results domain {Inspected, Pass, Fail}, same code uniqueness rules. (9) update_checklist / list_checklists / archive_checklist parallel to workflow ops. (10) add_checklist_item / update_checklist_item / delete_checklist_item for flat checklists. (11) search_workflows(ctx, q, page, page_size) route GET /workflows/search: text search WITHIN individual workflow items (not just headers), return Page of SearchHit with matched item snippets. (12) search_checklists similarly. (13) snapshot(workflow_id|checklist_id) -> TemplateSnapshot{template_id, kind:workflow|checklist, code, items:list[WorkItemSnapshot], frozen_at}: freeze template state for work order generation, called by WORKORDERS on generation. (14) validate_item_graph(items) ensuring predecessor references are valid and acyclic, measurement fields match data_type {NUMERIC, TEXT, BOOLEAN}. Events: template.created, template.updated, template.archived. Depends on core, db, api.

chunks.name: Cycles - Maintenance Cycle Engine
chunks.description: Cycle CRUD, triggers (calendar/hours/count), winner logic, suspension, missed-cycle detection, idempotent evaluation emitting cycle.due events.
chunks.prompt: Implement CYCLES module at /src/server/modules/cycles/ with tables: cycles, cycle_triggers, cycle_evaluations. Functions: (1) create_cycle(ctx, data) route POST /cycles (MANAGER): validate target entity exists via ASSETS, validate template exists via TEMPLATES, validate cron expressions, persist cycle + triggers, emit cycle.created, audited. Data includes {code?, name, description, target_entity_type:ZONE|SYSTEM|SUB_SYSTEM|SERVICE_POINT, target_entity_id, assigned_template_id, safety_flag?, deadline, grace_period, deadline_behavior:FLAG_CRITICAL_STOP|WAIT_UNTIL_COMPLETED, launch_mode:AUTOMATIC|MANUAL, auto_frequency?, postpone_overhead?, influence_child_nodes, triggers[]}. (2) update_cycle(ctx, cycle_id, patch) route PATCH /cycles/{id} (MANAGER): changes apply ONLY to newly generated work orders, existing WOs keep snapshots, audited, emit cycle.updated. (3) list_cycles(ctx, filters, page, page_size) route GET /cycles: org-scoped list. (4) get_cycle(ctx, cycle_id) route GET /cycles/{id}: cycle + triggers + last evaluations. (5) add_trigger / update_trigger / remove_trigger routes POST|PATCH|DELETE /cycles/{id}/triggers[/{triggerId}]: multiple triggers per cycle, trigger spec {type:CALENDAR|HOURS|COUNT, cron?|threshold?}. (6) suspend_cycle(ctx, cycle_id) route POST /cycles/{id}/suspend (MANAGER): status SUSPENDED, no WO generation, calendar triggers pause, emit cycle.suspended, audited. (7) activate_cycle(ctx, cycle_id) route POST /cycles/{id}/activate (MANAGER): SUSPENDED->ACTIVE, next evaluation resumes, emit cycle.activated, audited. (8) archive_cycle(ctx, cycle_id) route DELETE /cycles/{id} (MANAGER): status ARCHIVED (soft), stops evaluation, history retained. (9) manual_trigger(ctx, cycle_id) route POST /cycles/{id}/manual-trigger (MANAGER): immediate evaluation for MANUAL launch mode, emit cycle.due with source=MANUAL, rate-limited, audited. (10) evaluate_due_cycles() task beat=every minute inside WORKER.single_flight: find ACTIVE cycles, skip SUSPENDED, evaluate calendar triggers (UTC), evaluate counter triggers via ASSETS.effective_counter, FIRST satisfied trigger wins, emit cycle.due{cycle_id, trigger_id, period_key} (WORKORDERS generates WO), write cycle_evaluations row, idempotency via CACHE.lock per cycle + unique(cycle_id, period_key), failures recorded + emit cycle.eval_failed. (11) evaluate_calendar(trigger, now_utc, last_run) -> bool: cron matching with auto_frequency (once/twice per day/shift), missed windows handled by detect_missed_cycles. (12) evaluate_counter(trigger, entity_id) -> bool: resolve ASSETS.effective_counter (inheritance), compare against threshold since last trigger, influence_child_nodes prevents child override. (13) detect_missed_cycles() task beat=every 5 minutes: calendar cycles past due without trigger -> emit cycle.missed (WORKORDERS creates overdue-flagged WO), emit telemetry. (14) get_evaluations(ctx, cycle_id, page, page_size) route GET /cycles/{id}/evaluations: evaluation log with trigger, result, generated WO id, errors. Events: cycle.created, cycle.updated, cycle.suspended, cycle.activated, cycle.due, cycle.missed, cycle.eval_failed. CRITICAL: CYCLES never calls WORKORDERS directly; it emits cycle.due events which WORKORDERS subscribes to. Depends on core, db, api, assets, templates, worker, cache.

chunks.name: Work Orders - Execution Engine
chunks.description: Work order lifecycle: generation from cycle.due events, acknowledge/reject/snooze, item execution, measurements, signatures, comments.
chunks.prompt: Implement WORKORDERS module at /src/server/modules/workorders/ with tables: work_orders, work_order_items, work_order_item_measurements, work_order_comments, work_order_signatures, snooze_records, rejection_records, work_order_attachments(join). Functions: (1) generate_from_cycle(cycle_id, trigger_ctx) subscriber for cycle.due/cycle.missed events: idempotent via unique(cycle_id, period_key), snapshot template via TEMPLATES.snapshot, target asset from ASSETS, deadline + grace from cycle, status GENERATED, if missed->overdue flag visible, emit work_order.generated, NOTIFY assignee. trigger_ctx={trigger_id, period_key, overdue:bool, source:AUTO|MANUAL|MISSED}. (2) list_work_orders(ctx, filters, page, page_size) route GET /work-orders: org-scoped, role-filtered (MAINTENANCE sees assigned/pool, MANAGER all). (3) get_work_order(ctx, wo_id) route GET /work-orders/{id}: full detail including snapshot items, measurements, comments, attachments, ASSETS.effective_flags, linked ticket, triggers acknowledge side-effect on first view. (4) acknowledge(ctx, wo_id) route POST /work-orders/{id}/acknowledge: idempotent, store viewed_by + first_view_at, GENERATED->ACKNOWLEDGED, emit work_order.acknowledged. (5) reject(ctx, wo_id, reason) route POST /work-orders/{id}/reject: status REJECTED, rejection_records row with REQUIRED non-empty reason, remains in history, emit work_order.rejected, notify manager. (6) snooze(ctx, wo_id, duration, reason) route POST /work-orders/{id}/snooze: duration in {1h,6h,12h,1d,3d,6d} exact set, reason REQUIRED, status SNOOZED, snooze_records row, CACHE.delay_schedule(resume task at now+duration), emit work_order.snoozed. (7) resume(ctx, wo_id): SNOOZED->previous active state, emit work_order.resumed. (8) resume_snoozed() task beat=every minute: pop CACHE.delay_due -> resume each + NTF snooze-expiration notification. (9) update_item(ctx, wo_id, item_id, patch) route PATCH /work-orders/{id}/items/{itemId} (MAINTENANCE,MANAGER): patch {status:TASK|STARTED|COMPLETED|FAILED|PENDING_PREDECESSOR|PERFORMED_BY, started_at, closed_at, performed_by, notes}, validate transitions incl. predecessor resolution (PENDING_PREDECESSOR releases when predecessor completes), recompute completion %, emit wo_item.updated. (10) record_measurement(ctx, wo_id, item_id, value) route POST /work-orders/{id}/items/{itemId}/measurement: type-check NUMERIC/TEXT/BOOLEAN against snapshot definition, store raw value (auto pass/fail from thresholds is post-MVP), emit wo_item.measured. (11) add_comment(ctx, wo_id, text, parent_comment_id=None) route POST /work-orders/{id}/comments: threaded comments. (12) attach_file(ctx, wo_id, file_id, item_id=None) route POST /work-orders/{id}/attachments: delegate FILES.attach for WO-level or item-level attachments. (13) sign(ctx, wo_id, item_id, signature) route POST /work-orders/{id}/items/{itemId}/signature: only when snapshot item requires digital signature, store signer + timestamp, emit wo_item.signed. (14) complete(ctx, wo_id, cost=None, downtime=None) route POST /work-orders/{id}/complete (MAINTENANCE): all items terminal, completion 100%, capture cost/downtime/finish time, status COMPLETED, emit work_order.completed, releases STOP_UNTIL_COMPLETE effects via ASSETS state recompute. (15) close(ctx, wo_id, quality_check_by=None) route POST /work-orders/{id}/close (MANAGER): COMPLETED->CLOSED with QC reviewer, emit work_order.closed. (16) flag_overdue() task beat=every 5 minutes: past-deadline active WOs -> OVERDUE + visible flag, apply deadline_behavior (FLAG_CRITICAL_STOP triggers ASSETS safety flag; WAIT_UNTIL_COMPLETED marks wait), emit work_order.overdue, NTF. (17) assert_transition(current, target) -> None: state machine table GENERATED->ACKNOWLEDGED->IN_PROGRESS->(BLOCKED|SNOOZED|REJECTED)->OVERDUE->COMPLETED->CLOSED, raise InvalidTransition. (18) recompute_completion(wo_id) -> int 0-100: derived from item states, persisted on WO. (19) for_node(ctx, node_id) -> WoNodeView: active + historical WOs for node, port used by QR resolve and MCP. Events: work_order.generated, acknowledged, rejected, snoozed, resumed, blocked, completed, closed, overdue, wo_item.updated, measured, signed. Depends on core, db, api, templates, assets, cache, files, worker.

chunks.name: Tickets - Repair Ticketing & Files
chunks.description: Repair ticket creation with payment gate, pool claim/assign, 5-step flow with 3-loop cap, escalation. File attachment domain with policy validation, ingestion flagging.
chunks.prompt: Implement TICKETS and FILES modules at /src/server/modules/{tickets,files}/. TICKETS tables: tickets, ticket_reports, ticket_feedbacks, ticket_assignments, ticket_events. Functions: (1) create_ticket(ctx, data) route POST /tickets (OPERATOR,MANAGER): Gate1 TENANCY.can_create_ticket (overdue orgs get error_code=ORG_PAYMENT_OVERDUE), Gate2 node ACTIVE (unless domain rule allows), create OPEN ticket routed to Maintenance Pool, attach files via FILES, ticket_events row, emit ticket.created, NTF notify_role(MAINTENANCE), audited. Data {service_point_id, report_section?, description, priority:LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH|CRITICAL, attachments[]}. (2) list_tickets(ctx, filters, page, page_size) route GET /tickets: org+role scoped. (3) get_ticket(ctx, ticket_id) route GET /tickets/{id}: ticket + reports + feedbacks + assignments + full event history. (4) claim(ctx, ticket_id) route POST /tickets/{id}/claim (MAINTENANCE): OPEN->IN_PROGRESS, assignment=claimant, ticket_assignments row, emit ticket.claimed, NTF issuer, audited. (5) assign(ctx, ticket_id, user_id) route POST /tickets/{id}/assign (MANAGER): manual assignment, reassignment audited, emit ticket.assigned, NTF assignee. (6) submit_report(ctx, ticket_id, report) route POST /tickets/{id}/report (MAINTENANCE): IN_PROGRESS->REPORT_SUBMITTED, ticket_reports row with work performed/findings/attachments, emit ticket.report_submitted, NTF issuer. (7) submit_feedback(ctx, ticket_id, feedback) route POST /tickets/{id}/feedback (issuer OPERATOR|MANAGER): REPORT_SUBMITTED->ISSUER_FEEDBACK_REQUIRED->back to IN_PROGRESS, loop_counter++, if loop_counter>3 auto-escalate, emit ticket.feedback_requested. (8) accept_ticket(ctx, ticket_id) route POST /tickets/{id}/accept (issuer): ->ISSUER_ACCEPTED then CLOSED, emit ticket.accepted + ticket.closed, NTF maintenance. (9) escalate(ctx, ticket_id) route POST /tickets/{id}/escalate (issuer,MANAGER,or auto): ->ESCALATED_TO_MANAGER, emit ticket.escalated, NTF managers. (10) manager_decision(ctx, ticket_id, decision, note) route POST /tickets/{id}/decision (MANAGER): decision in {FORCE_CLOSE, REQUIRE_NEW_TICKET, MANDATE_ACTION} resolving escalation per baseline 12. (11) assert_transition(current, target): 5-step state machine OPEN->IN_PROGRESS->REPORT_SUBMITTED->ISSUER_FEEDBACK_REQUIRED->ISSUER_ACCEPTED->CLOSED with ESCALATED_TO_MANAGER branch, raise InvalidTransition. (12) loop_guard(ticket) -> bool: persisted loop counter for steps 3<->4, max 3 repetitions. (13) for_node(ctx, node_id) -> TicketNodeView: active + historical tickets for node. FILES tables: files, work_order_attachments(join semantics shared). Functions: (1) validate_upload(filename, mime_claimed, size, head) -> violation codes {MIME_INVALID, EXT_BLOCKED, SIZE_EXCEEDED, EXECUTABLE_BLOCKED}: allowed JPEG/PNG/PDF/TXT/DOCX (+config), max 10MB default, BOTH extension and MIME checked, sniffed MIME must match claimed, executables blocked. (2) upload(ctx, stream, meta) route POST /files/upload (multipart): validate_upload -> STORAGE.tenant_key -> STORAGE.put -> persist metadata row {original_name, key, mime, size, uploaded_by, entity_type, entity_id, purpose:ATTACHMENT|MANUAL|PHOTO|EXPORT|AI_INGESTION_ARTIFACT}, emit file.uploaded, audited, rate-limited. (3) get_file(ctx, file_id) route GET /files/{id}: org+permission check on linked entity. (4) download_url(ctx, file_id) route GET /files/{id}/download-url: verify caller org + entity permission -> STORAGE.presigned_url (15 min). (5) delete_file(ctx, file_id) route DELETE /files/{id}: soft-delete metadata, STORAGE.delete, blocked where retention/audit requires, emit file.deleted, audited. (6) list_for_entity(ctx, entity_type, entity_id, purpose=None): all files linked to entity (node manuals, WO attachments, ticket attachments). (7) attach(ctx, entity_type, entity_id, file_id): link existing file to entity, THE port used by WORKORDERS/TICKETS/ASSETS. (8) mark_for_ingestion(ctx, file_id) route POST /files/{id}/ingest (MANAGER,MAINTENANCE): only PDF/TXT/DOCX, set ingestion_status=PENDING, emit manual.ingestion_requested{file_id, org_id, node_id}, AI module consumes. (9) set_ingestion_status(file_id, status): port for AI callbacks, status in {PENDING,PROCESSING,COMPLETED,FAILED}. (10) duplicate_policy(ctx, content_hash, entity_type, entity_id) -> DupDecision{reject|version|allow}: org-configured duplicate handling. Events: ticket.created, claimed, assigned, report_submitted, feedback_requested, accepted, escalated, closed; file.uploaded, deleted, manual.ingestion_requested. TICKETS depends on core,db,api,assets,tenancy. FILES depends on core,db,api,storage,tenancy.

chunks.name: AI Module - Checklist Generation & RAG Assistant
chunks.description: AI subsystem: provider abstraction (OpenRouter/OpenAI/Anthropic/local), Phase 1 checklist generation, Phase 2 RAG manual assistant with pgvector embeddings.
chunks.prompt: Implement AI module at /src/server/modules/ai/ with internal structure: ports.py (AIGateway protocol), providers/ (openrouter.py, openai.py, anthropic.py, local.py adapters), checklist/ (generation service + JSON-schema validation), rag/ (ingestion pipeline + retrieval + assistant), usage.py (logs, quotas, rate limits, prompt sanitizer). Tables: document_ingestion_jobs, document_chunks(+embedding), ai_generation_jobs, ai_assistant_threads, ai_assistant_messages, ai_usage_logs. Functions: (1) provider() -> AIGateway selecting adapter by CMMS_AI__PROVIDER (openrouter|openai|anthropic|local), each implementing generate_text(prompt, model, max_tokens, temperature, timeout) and embed(texts, model). Adapters handle timeouts/retries/model names; local adapter for Ollama/vLLM self-hosted. (2) sanitize_prompt(text) -> str: strip org_id, PII, tenant identifiers before sending externally. (3) generate_checklist(ctx, prompt, node_id=None) route POST /ai/checklists/generate: validate prompt length, sanitize, call provider with schema-enforced JSON output for checklist structure, retry on invalid JSON up to 3 times, create ai_generation_jobs row {status:PROCESSING}, return job_id. (4) generate_checklist_async(job_id) task: execute generation, validate against JSON schema, persist result, status COMPLETED|FAILED, emit ai.checklist_completed/failed, NTF. (5) get_generation(ctx, job_id) route GET /ai/generations/{id}: return generation status + result. (6) ingest_manual(file_id) task: consume manual.ingestion_requested event, fetch file via STORAGE, extract text (PDF/txt/docx), chunk with metadata {organization_id, service_point_id, file_id, page, chunk_index, heading, tokens}, embed via provider, upsert to pgvector document_chunks with organization_id filter, update document_ingestion_jobs status, emit ai.ingestion_completed/failed. (7) retry_failed_ingestions() task beat=~10 min: retry failed ingestion jobs. (8) ask_assistant(ctx, thread_id, question) route POST /ai/assistant/threads/{id}/messages: retrieve top-k chunks from pgvector filtered by organization_id + service_point_id (if thread bound to node), similarity threshold, ground answer with citations, fallback "not found in manuals", persist ai_assistant_messages, emit ai.assistant_answered, support SSE streaming. (9) create_thread(ctx, node_id=None) route POST /ai/assistant/threads: create thread optionally bound to node. (10) get_messages(ctx, thread_id) route GET /ai/assistant/threads/{id}/messages: return thread history. (11) reprocess_manual(ctx, file_id) route POST /ai/manuals/{fileId}/reprocess (MANAGER,MAINTENANCE): re-run ingestion. (12) log_usage(org_id, user_id, operation, tokens_in, tokens_out): persist to ai_usage_logs for quota tracking. Events consumed: manual.ingestion_requested. Events emitted: ai.checklist_requested/completed/failed, ai.ingestion_completed/failed, ai.assistant_answered. Config: CMMS_AI__PROVIDER, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_BASE_URL, CHAT_MODEL, EMBEDDING_MODEL, TIMEOUT, MAX_RETRIES, PRIVACY_MODE_ORGS (force local adapter), RATE_LIMIT_AI_* (stricter limits via CACHE). Health: adapter reachability probe (tiny completion/embedding ping), pgvector readiness, ingestion queue depth. Depends on core, db (pgvector), api, cache (rate limits), worker, storage.

chunks.name: MCP Server - External AI Agent Interface
chunks.description: MCP server exposing full CMMS surface to external AI agents: resources (read), tools (write), prompts, with mandatory guardrails (confirmation gates, dry-run, rate limits, ceilings, rollback).
chunks.prompt: Implement MCP module at /src/server/modules/mcp/ using official MCP Python SDK. Functions: (1) create_server() -> McpServer: initialize MCP SDK server, advertise supported spec versions, reject unsupported clients, register health on HTTP transport. (2) serve_stdio(): stdio transport for local/sidecar agents. (3) serve_http(port=8100): Streamable HTTP/SSE transport behind nginx /mcp/*, restricted network, MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS enforced. (4) authenticate(credential) -> Session{org_id, role, actor_id, key_id}: JWT path uses AUTH.verify_access_token; API-key path looks up scoped key bound to one organization_id + one role; SYS_ADMIN REJECTED unconditionally; unauthenticated calls blocked before any tool/resource. (5) authorize(session, required_roles): per-call role gate mirroring REST RBAC, protocol error on denial. (6) register_resources(server): register read resources cmms://assets/zones, cmms://assets/systems, cmms://assets/service-points/{id}, .../history, .../manuals, cmms://cycles/{id}, cmms://workflows/{id}, cmms://checklists/{id}, cmms://work-orders, cmms://work-orders/{id}, cmms://tickets, cmms://tickets/{id}, cmms://reports/kpis, cmms://notifications - each maps to owning module's port with org scope + role check. (7) register_tools(server): register write tools wrapping domain ports (NO re-implementation): Asset(MANAGER): create_zone, update_zone, clone_zone, decommission_zone, create_system, update_system, create_service_point, update_service_point, generate_qr, decommission_service_point. Cycles(MANAGER): create_cycle, update_cycle, suspend_cycle, activate_cycle, assign_workflow_to_cycle, assign_checklist_to_cycle, set_cycle_flag. Counters(OPERATOR,MANAGER): log_operating_hours, log_operation_count, reset_counter. WorkOrders(MAINTENANCE,MANAGER): acknowledge_work_order, reject_work_order, snooze_work_order, update_work_order_item_status, record_measurement, submit_work_order_signature, add_work_order_comment. Tickets(OPERATOR,MANAGER,MAINTENANCE): create_repair_ticket, submit_ticket_report, submit_ticket_feedback, accept_ticket, escalate_ticket. Authoring(MANAGER): create_workflow, create_checklist, add_workflow_item, add_checklist_item, ai_generate_checklist. AI(any authed): ask_manual_assistant. Reporting(MANAGER,REPORTER): get_kpi_dashboard, export_report. Ops: batch_rollback. (8) register_prompts(server): prompt://cycle-analysis, prompt://overdue-triage, prompt://root-cause, prompt://zone-onboarding with parameter placeholders. (9) confirmation_gate(session, tool, args) -> PendingConfirmation|None: MANDATORY gates for set_cycle_flag(STOP_UNTIL_COMPLETE), decommission_zone, decommission_service_point, clone_zone, create_repair_ticket(priority=CRITICAL); execution proceeds only via confirm(token) presented to human; CMMS_MCP__CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED=true default. (10) apply_dry_run(tool, args) -> DryRunResult|None: every write tool accepts dry_run:true, validate inputs, compute side-effects, return {would_persist:[...], validation:ok|errors} WITHOUT persisting. (11) rate_limit(session, tool): via CACHE.allow, write tools max 30/min/session, AI-assist tools max 10/min/session, plus global REST limiter inheritance. (12) ceiling(session, tool): session-hour caps <=50 work orders, <=50 tickets; exceed -> quota error. (13) safety_flag_guard(session, tool, args): MCP agent cannot clear/downgrade a STOP_UNTIL_COMPLETE flag set by human; escalation only, raise on violation. (14) batch_rollback(session, n): undo last N session writes within window (default 5 min, CMMS_MCP__ROLLBACK_WINDOW_S) ONLY if no human modified those records since; transactional, return {rolled_back:int, skipped:[{reason}]}. (15) audit_call(session, tool, args, result): AUDIT.record with actor_type=MCP_AGENT, actor_id=session/key_id, action=tool, input_hash=sha256(payload), ip/user-agent of orchestrator, powers org-level "AI Activity Log". (16) health_check() -> HealthReport: transport liveness + auth bridge self-test + downstream port reachability, served at /health on HTTP transport. Config: MCP_TRANSPORT=stdio|http, MCP_HTTP_PORT=8100, MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS, MCP_MAX_BATCH_SIZE=50, MCP_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED=true, MCP_DRY_RUN_DEFAULT=false. Depends on core, auth, tenancy, assets, cycles, templates, workorders, tickets, reports, ai, cache.

global_notes.build_order: Modules must be built in wave order (0->6). Within a wave, follow priority order from Server-module-function-list.json. A module may only import modules from earlier waves or same wave with lower priority number.
global_notes.testing_strategy: Build functional implementation first. Add unit/integration tests after each chunk reaches stable state. Contract tests for adapters (storage/email/AI providers) ensure swap safety.
global_notes.infrastructure_setup: Docker Compose with services: api (FastAPI), worker (Celery), beat (Celery Beat), mcp (MCP server), db (PostgreSQL 15+pgvector), redis (Redis 7), minio (S3-compatible), nginx (reverse proxy routing /api/* to api, /mcp/* to mcp). No UI server in this repo - UI is separate React SPA consuming REST API.
global_notes.source_layout: All code under /src/server/: core/ (kernel), modules/{db,cache,storage,email,api,worker,auth,tenancy,assets,templates,cycles,workorders,tickets,files,ai,mcp}/, shared/ (enums, events_catalog, errors, ids), migrations/ (Alembic stamped per module), entrypoints/ (api.py, worker.py, beat.py, mcp.py, all_in_one.py)

key_conventions.request_context: Every domain service function takes ctx: RequestContext as first param. RequestContext = {org_id: UUID, user_id: UUID, role: Role, request_id: str, timezone: str|None}. HTTP routes build it from verified JWT.
key_conventions.ids: UUID v4 for all business records
key_conventions.timestamps: ISO 8601 UTC, stored as timestamptz, user timezone applied at display only
key_conventions.pagination: Page[T] = {items: list[T], page: int, page_size: int, total: int}
key_conventions.events: Dot-delimited names; published via core.publish(); consumers never know producers
key_conventions.rls: All tenant queries run inside db.org_scoped_session(org_id) setting PostgreSQL RLS
key_conventions.soft_delete: No hard deletes of business records; use deleted_at + is_active + lifecycle_status
key_conventions.audit: Functions marked 'audited' emit an audit event consumed by AUDIT module (AUDIT implemented as event listener in later phase)
